- B.5 `code-intel-enforcer.ts` (PreToolUse on `Bash|mcp__serena__*`) in **warn mode** — `CCV3_FACADE_MODE=warn` default. Logs would-route events to intel-bus.

findings.title: proposed_bus_updates is produced by the facade but has zero consumers: the always-in-context boundary rule claims a 'downstream SubagentStop writer' in present tense, yet no SubagentStop hook is registered anywhere and no hooks/src file references proposed_bus_updates — codegraph results never reach the bus

evidence.quote: A downstream `SubagentStop` writer revalidates before applying; stale proposals are dropped. The facade never mutates `context.json`.

// TTL/validity stamp -- a downstream SubagentStop writer revalidates before
      // applying. Stale (HEAD moved or corpus drifted) -> the proposal is dropped.

findings.telemetry: rg 'proposed_bus_updates' over .claude/hooks/src/ returns no matches (exit 1); rg 'SubagentStop' over .claude/settings.json and ~/.claude/settings.json returns no registrations. Every proposal is therefore dropped — not by revalidation, but by the consumer not existing. Consequence: the bus's focus_symbols never receive codegraph data, so the B.3 recall-biasing readers (memory-awareness/agent-recall) run on a starved bus (focus_count 0 in most live *_bus_read rows).
causal_links: D1b-01 (handoff-loss metric has no write-side event because this writer is missing)
memory-recall 27.4% hit-rate context: bus biasing cannot improve while the bus never receives specialist output

evidence.quote: Each codegraph call pays a ~3-4s Node+WASM startup tax — amortized by the freshness cache, never by making codegraph faster.
